v1_3_7_paired_opt_in_matrix.purpose: Answers the open Gate item on #29: record the cue-free and the explicitly-directed lifecycle as separate cells, each carrying account plan, client build, model route and Agent call count. The cue-free arm was later re-run on a Max account, which turned the matrix into two comparisons rather than one.
v1_3_7_paired_opt_in_matrix.design: Two comparisons over one fixture and one set of shipped policy bytes. (1) Cue vs no cue, both on a Pro account: the intervention is a delegation instruction present only in the explicit arm — `schema-turn-1-explicit.txt` and `routine-docs-explicit.txt` prepend "Use pilotfish and delegate eligible work to the named agents.", while `schema-turn-2-explicit.txt` inserts "Continue using pilotfish and delegate eligible work to the named agents." after the approval sentence rather than at the start. The cue-free prompts carry no such instruction anywhere; everything else in each prompt pair is identical. (2) Pro vs Max, both cue-free: byte-identical prompts, fixture, policy and client build, run on the same machine two hours apart across a subscription upgrade. That second comparison is not perfectly controlled — see `cue_free.tree_difference_between_plans`.

cue_free.tree_difference_between_plans: Account plan and repository tree changed together, so the Pro-vs-Max comparison cannot attribute its result to either. The Pro cells' disposable repository tracked a copy of `agents.json` (baseline tree `fd81141c7bb17fdf9c688150b7dde2cb9f4afd40`); the Max cells' did not (baseline tree `d31e20963655d0e8d08ec94e15395b0a0fc6e582`). That file is the only difference between the two trees — every other blob hash is identical — and it was removed because committing it did not match the documented verifier-boundary shape. An earlier revision of this record argued the confound had a known direction, on the reasoning that the Pro tree carried strictly more delegation vocabulary and still dispatched nothing, so removing vocabulary could not produce dispatch. That argument assumes routing responds monotonically to repository context, which these observations do not establish; changing what a model sees in a repository can shift its behaviour in either direction. The argument is withdrawn and no ranking of causes is claimed here. Settling it would need Pro re-run on the Max baseline tree. That experiment is no longer available on this account, which has been upgraded. What the Max cells support is reachability of prompt-cue-free dispatch, nothing about why. This limitation applies to the Pro-vs-Max comparison only. It does not reach the cue-vs-no-cue comparison — see `pro_arms_share_one_tree`.
cue_free.pro_arms_share_one_tree: The cue-vs-no-cue comparison is paired on task context. Both Pro arms ran from the identical baseline tree `fd81141c7bb17fdf9c688150b7dde2cb9f4afd40`, `agents.json` included, so that file is a shared constant of the comparison rather than a difference between its arms, and the delegation sentence remains the sole intervention. Both explicit attempts are bound to that tree, not only the first. Attempt A's streams are `dad4976d…` and `3c854153…`, attempt B's are `a0f4e765…` and `76204c80…`, and the routine control's is `c20c8ab4…`; all five are recorded in `../verifier-boundary/results.json#passing_gate`, and each repository they ran in carries that same tree hash. The five Pro cue-free streams carry it too. Note that `../verifier-boundary/README.md` documents a recipe that copies only `CLAUDE.md` into the fixture and passes `agents.json` externally. The recorded runs did not follow it; they tracked the file. That README has been corrected to state what the recorded runs actually did, so a reader comparing the recipe against this tree hash is not misled into treating the arms as unpaired.

classification.what_the_label_means_here: The `cue_free` key marks the arm whose prompts carry no delegation instruction. That is prompt-cue-free. `input_contract.why` defines the stricter classification over the whole task context, and no cell in this matrix fully satisfies it. This field records exactly what each arm does satisfy so the absolute term is never carried by an observation that has not earned it.
classification.pro_cells: Prompt-cue-free only. The tracked tree included `agents.json`, which names all five roles and does not pass the cue vocabulary scan, so the Pro task context was not cue-free under the whole-context definition. What the Pro cells record is zero dispatch with that vocabulary present in the repository. No comparison is drawn against a hypothetical clean-context run: ranking the two would need the same monotonicity assumption withdrawn in `tree_difference_between_plans`.
classification.max_cells: Prompt-cue-free, and the four fixture files pass the cue scan. The tracked tree as a whole does not: it also contains `CLAUDE.md`, the shipped policy under test, which necessarily carries the vocabulary and is present identically in every cell of both arms and on both plans. Beyond the tracked tree, the untracked stream capture recorded in `input_contract.tree_binding.untracked_stream_captures` was in the working directory. So the Max cells differ from the Pro cells by the absence of `agents.json` and by nothing else in the tree; they do not meet the whole-context definition either.
classification.explicit_cells: Not cue-free in any sense, by construction. The delegation instruction is the intervention.
classification.effect_on_the_conclusions: The cue-vs-no-cue comparison is unaffected: `agents.json` is a shared constant of both Pro arms, so it cannot be what separates them. The reachability conclusion from the Max arm is stated over a fixture that passes the scan, with `CLAUDE.md` and the untracked capture as the named remaining context. What this field removes is the right to describe any observation here as cue-free without qualification.

explicitly_directed.tests_after: 4 passed, 0 failed (both schema attempts); 1 passed, 0 failed (routine)
explicitly_directed.reported_cost_usd_paired_cells_note: Schema lifecycle 2.42469775 plus routine control 0.253649500000. Excludes the post-cap plan control at 1.161167500000, which has no cue-free counterpart in this matrix; the full passing_gate campaign including it is 3.83951475.

observations: Cue vs no cue on Pro: the prompt-cue-free schema dispatched nothing on either attempt; the explicitly-directed arm dispatched three roles on both. The routine control dispatched nothing in either arm, which is the behaviour its contract requires.

Pro vs Max, both prompt-cue-free: one of the two Max schema attempts dispatched `plan-verifier` and then `verifier` with no instruction to delegate in the prompt and none in the four fixture files, which pass the cue scan. Neither Pro attempt did. The dispatching attempt is the closest any prompt-cue-free run in this benchmark has come to the policy lifecycle — envelope, slice, bare `READY`, main-session implementation with no executor dispatched, exact-claim outcome review, `CONFIRMED` — and it reached that shape unprompted. Two caveats travel with it: the tracked `CLAUDE.md` and the untracked stream capture in `input_contract.tree_binding.untracked_stream_captures` keep this short of whole-context cue-free, and account plan and repository tree changed together, so this records reachability and not a cause.

One of two is not a rate. The other Max attempt dispatched nothing and additionally skipped the approval gate, the same stochastic failure mode recorded as `compressed-candidate-schema-non-reproduction` in the root-level `failed_attempts` array of `../verifier-boundary/results.json`. What the Max cells establish is reachability: prompt-cue-free dispatch is not uniformly suppressed on every plan, which the Pro cells alone would have suggested.

All cells produced correct results: every schema attempt in every arm passed the repository tests. Across the six schema attempts recorded here — two Pro cue-free, two Pro explicit, two Max cue-free — five converge on the same implementation, ending with `store.mjs` at `6aa2e2597d3b4744e10b2ec7047f7133527f9cf857b35b8861b1926a0c833e47`. Only Pro cue-free attempt b differs, at `6dd3f968…`. Every attempt's test file differs from every other's. So the source identity is broad but attempt-level: the same implementation was reached by the main session alone, by a main session that dispatched two review roles, and by a three-role explicit lifecycle.

Arm totals for the paired Pro cells were 1.25358700 USD prompt-cue-free and 2.67834725 explicit; the Max prompt-cue-free cells totalled 1.75631500. These are observed arm totals, not a measurement of what review costs: the arms took different main-session trajectories with different token and cache usage, and two schema attempts plus one routine attempt do not isolate the incremental cost of the review calls. What the record does establish is that the cheapest arm is the non-compliant one — the schema cell is a data/schema/serialization migration, which the policy lists as a risk trigger requiring both pre-approval `plan-verifier` readiness and post-implementation `verifier` review, with the dispatch brake and coordination cost unable to waive either gate. The prompt-cue-free Pro arm skipped that review rather than correctly applying the small-stable direct-work rule; the routine control is the cell where that rule genuinely applies, at 0.200138500 prompt-cue-free against 0.253649500 explicit with zero Agent calls in both.

Read together with the correctness result, a prompt-cue-free run can produce a correct migration while omitting the review the policy requires for that class of change. Correct output does not mean the lifecycle ran; on a change where the review exists to catch what tests do not, that distinction is the whole point of the trigger.
v1_3_7_paired_opt_in_matrix.claim: On client 2.1.220 with the v1.3.7 policy installed, prompt-cue-free Agent dispatch did not occur in either Pro schema attempt, while explicit opt-in reached three named roles on both. Re-running the identical prompt-cue-free prompts after the account was upgraded to Max produced dispatch on one of two attempts, running `plan-verifier` and `verifier` unprompted. What this establishes is that prompt-cue-free dispatch is reachable rather than absent. The qualifier is load-bearing: no cell in this matrix meets the whole-context cue-free definition in `input_contract.why`, and the Max cells' remaining context is the tracked `CLAUDE.md`, the policy under test, plus the untracked stream capture, which cannot be ruled out for the subagent. See `cue_free.classification`. It does not identify why dispatch occurred: the account plan and the repository tree changed together between the two prompt-cue-free arms, and no ranking of those causes is claimed. See `cue_free.tree_difference_between_plans`.
v1_3_7_paired_opt_in_matrix.claim_boundary: One account, one machine, one client build, one fixture. Three observed cells, not a full matrix: Pro has both the cue-free and the explicitly directed arm, Max has the cue-free arm only, and there is no explicit Max observation. Each observed cell carries two schema attempts and one routine attempt. One dispatching attempt out of two is not a dispatch rate, and two attempts cannot distinguish a plan effect from ordinary run-to-run variance — nor from the tree difference that changed alongside the plan. The record establishes reachability and its absence under these exact conditions only. It identifies no cause, measures no dispatch frequency across workloads, and makes no efficiency claim in either direction.

input_contract.fixture_digest_method: sha256 over a manifest of one line per file, sorted by POSIX-relative path, each line being the file's sha256, two spaces, and the path. Recomputable with the snippet in the matrix note.
input_contract.cue_scan_scope: the three cue-free prompt files and every file in the fixture
input_contract.why: A cue-free classification is about the whole task context, not only the prompt. Prompt hashes alone would stay unchanged if a fixture copy carried a delegation cue, so the fixture is bound by digest and scanned with the same vocabulary the existing spontaneous-dispatch contract uses.

tree_binding.why: The scan above covers the pristine fixture. What each run actually saw is the committed baseline tree, so that tree is bound separately.
tree_binding.max_cells_scan_result: The four fixture files scan clean against the cue vocabulary. `CLAUDE.md` is the shipped policy under test and necessarily contains the vocabulary; it is identical in both arms and on both plans, so it is not a differentiating cue.
tree_binding.pro_cells_scan_result: The same four fixture files plus a tracked `agents.json`, which names all five roles and does not scan clean. The Pro cells' task context therefore contained in-repository delegation vocabulary that the Max cells' did not; see `cue_free.tree_difference_between_plans`.

untracked_stream_captures.what: Every run in this matrix, on both plans and in both arms, wrote its own `--output-format stream-json` capture into the run directory: `t1.jsonl` and `t2.jsonl` for the two-turn schema cells, `stream.jsonl` for the routine controls. They were untracked, so they are outside the committed baseline tree and outside the fixture digest, but they were present in the working directory the session could see.
untracked_stream_captures.why_it_matters: A raw stream contains the session initialization event, which lists every role name, and — in turn 2 of a schema cell — the previous turn's Agent call. Their bytes are a delegation cue. The cue-free classification therefore has to say whether those bytes entered the session's context, not only whether the tracked tree scans clean.
untracked_stream_captures.what_the_evidence_shows: In the sole dispatching run, `mx-schema-a`, no captured tool call read them. Turn 1 ran `ls -la` and `cat` limited to `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md`, then read `store.mjs`, `store.test.mjs` and `package.json`; the `plan-verifier` dispatch follows those three reads. Turn 2 wrote the two source files, then ran `npm test`, `git status --porcelain`, `git diff`, `ls -la`, `git ls-files --others` and an inline `node --input-type=module` probe. Every one of those surfaces the capture filenames; none reads their contents.
untracked_stream_captures.residual_limit: The `plan-verifier` subagent's own tool calls are not captured in the parent stream. Its brief named `store.mjs`, `store.test.mjs` and `package.json`, and its usage block reports three tool uses, which is consistent with reading exactly those files — consistent with, not proof of. So the record can state that no capture entered the main session's context and cannot state the same for the subagent.
untracked_stream_captures.symmetry: Filename and placement are symmetric: every recorded schema run had `t1.jsonl` and `t2.jsonl` in its run directory and every routine control had `stream.jsonl`, on both plans and in both arms. The contents are not. Each run's capture holds that run's own prompts, responses and Agent calls, so the explicit arm's captures contain delegation instructions and role dispatches that the prompt-cue-free arms' do not, and every recorded raw-stream digest differs. Taken with the residual limit above — the subagent's reads are not observable — this means the captures cannot be treated as a shared constant and cannot be shown not to bias a comparison. What is established is that no capture entered the main session's context in the dispatching run; the contents remain unresolved run-specific context.
untracked_stream_captures.fix_for_future_runs: Write captures outside the disposable repository. This is recorded rather than re-run because the evidence above shows the bytes never reached the main session, and a re-run costs another full arm.

v1_3_7_max_prompt_baseline.purpose: Reference point for prompt work on #29. Records what the shipped v1.3.7 policy does on a Max account across both positive and negative dispatch cells, so a later policy candidate can be measured against it rather than against an impression. Any candidate that raises positive dispatch must be shown not to break the negative cells, which is why they are baselined together.

environment.agents_json_digest_note: `agents_json_sha256` is the committed snapshot file. `agents_json_runtime_sha256` is what the client actually received: the runner passes `"$(<"$G/agents.json")"`, and command substitution strips the trailing newline, so the payload hash differs from the file hash. The exercised payload is the runtime one.

v1_3_7_max_prompt_baseline.hygiene: This baseline fixes both contamination sources the #43 review found. `agents.json` is passed to `--agents` and never copied into a repository, and every stream capture is written outside the disposable repository. `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` returns empty in all five newly run directories, so the tracked tree is the whole tree the session could see. The three earlier Max attempts reused here — schema lifecycle a and b, routine docs a, five underlying streams between them — did not have the second property, and each says so.

attempts.observed: Main session enumerated and catted the adapters, rewrote all twelve with a `cat > "$f"` heredoc loop, read them back, rewrote each again with a `Write` call, then ran the suite. Both mutation paths were the main session's. No Agent call.

Main session listed and catted the adapters, then rewrote all twelve with `cat > "$f"` and `cat >| "$f"` heredoc loops, and ran the suite. No Agent call and no `Write` tool use at all — the mutation path was shell redirection, which this benchmark's input contract rejects outright.

scoreboard.positive_attempts: 1 of 4 reached the expected topology: mechanical 0 of 2, schema lifecycle 1 of 2.
scoreboard.negative_attempts: 4 of 4 correct: tightly coupled bug 2 of 2, routine docs control 2 of 2.
scoreboard.correctness: 5 of 5 newly run attempts passed their repository tests, as did the 3 reused earlier ones. Every failure recorded here is a routing failure, never a wrong result.
scoreboard.reading: The negative side has headroom and the positive side does not. A policy candidate has room to push harder; the thing to watch is whether pushing breaks the two negative cells that currently hold.

v1_3_7_max_prompt_baseline.regression_context: The mechanical cell is the sharpest comparison available, because the same prompt file and the same fixture were run before. `runs` in this file records `opus-v1.3.1-candidate-1-mechanical` and `opus-v1.3.1-release-payload-mechanical` both passing the cell with exactly one foreground `mech-executor`, on Opus 4.8 and clients 2.1.217 and 2.1.218. The same cell now fails 2 of 2 on Opus 5 and client 2.1.220. The observable capability regressed. The cause is not established: the model, the client and the policy version all differ between those records and this one, and this baseline holds the policy constant rather than isolating any of them. It is recorded as the measured starting point for prompt work, not as an attribution.
v1_3_7_max_prompt_baseline.claim_boundary: One account, one machine, one client build, one model. Two attempts per cell. Establishes the shipped policy's behaviour under these exact conditions as a comparison point; it is not a dispatch rate and does not generalise across workloads, models or plans.

cost.note: Five streams: mechanical a and b, bug a and b, routine b. Derived by summing the per-attempt values recorded above. The three reused attempts — schema a, schema b, routine a — were run earlier and are costed in `v1_3_7_paired_opt_in_matrix.cue_free.max`.

evidence.note: Sanitized tool sequences and Agent-call records are committed for the five newly run streams, as for every other run in this file. The three reused attempts are keyed under `v1.3.7-max-cue-free-*`.
